entries.value: Display language of the MAH Addressable editor tools (windows, inspectors and logs). This setting is personal to you. To add a language, put MAH.AddressableManager.Editor.<language code>.json under Assets (export a template with MAH/Addressable/Localization/Export Translation Template).
Change the language code in the file name to the language you are translating, then save (e.g. MAH.AddressableManager.Editor.fr.json).

Removes the leaks so far from this tab's view. The records themselves are not deleted; only leaks that occur afterwards are shown.

Writes the leaks currently shown to a text file (the output folder can be changed under "Leak" in AddressableEditorSettings). After exporting, press "Clear view" to make the next log contain only what happens afterwards.

The group count is the number of groups of the parents (registered assets) that use the child. Usage through registered assets is also counted (this does not mean the asset is duplicated in a build).
The size is the file size on disk, which differs from the size inside a bundle and from memory on a device.
For build reference: in a Pack Separately group, an asset can be included more than once even within the same group (marked in the list; use Addressables Analyze for an accurate check).

Interval (seconds) at which the window re-reads the running state. The lower limit is 0.1 seconds.
Output folder of the log. A relative path starts from the project root (the parent of Assets); an absolute path is used as is. If empty, the default is restored.
When Play ends, the leaks are exported automatically to AddressableLeaks_LastPlay.txt (only one previous file is kept, as AddressableLeaks_LastPlay-prev.txt).
Output folder of the text export. A relative path starts from the project root (the parent of Assets); an absolute path is used as is. If empty, the default is restored.
Turns auto registration on or off. When off, auto registration (AssetPostprocessor) does nothing and all rule SOs are ignored. Manual bulk registration is not affected.
Detail level of the auto registration log. Conflicts, duplicate addresses and warnings are shown in either mode.
Initial value when a rule is created: address template. It is copied when a rule SO is created, and also used as the initial value of the manual bulk registration window.
Initial value when a rule is created: labels (macros can be used). If empty, no label is added.
Initial value when a rule is created: exclude patterns (glob).
Name of the group used by manual bulk registration when no target group is specified. If empty, the Addressables DefaultGroup is used. Not used by rule SOs (auto registration).
The Addressables Group Template used to create a new group when the target group does not exist. If empty, the Addressables default template is used. A template set in a rule SO takes precedence.
How CheckUpdateAsync handles the catalog. None: neither check nor update / CheckOnly: check only / CheckAndUpdate: check and update. HasUpdateAsync never updates the catalog, whichever is set.
The labels targeted by HasUpdateAsync / CheckUpdateAsync / DownloadAsync when called without arguments. A label passed as a method argument takes precedence.
Number of retries on failure (0 to 10), counted per stage (check, update, size calculation, download).
Wait time before a retry (milliseconds, 0 to 60000).
Whether to delete the cache of old bundles that are no longer used when the catalog is updated. Keep it OFF until you have checked how it interacts with bundles that are being loaded.
Auto: initialization starts in the Manager's Awake. Manual: it does not start until InitializeAsync is called.
How Load is handled when it is called before initialization succeeds. After initialization fails, Load is stopped in either mode.
The value passed to autoReleaseHandle of Addressables.InitializeAsync. When OFF, the handle is released in Dispose.
Adds a per-request query to the URL of the remote catalog (.hash) so that the OS URL cache does not return an old catalog (for iOS / macOS).
Interval (seconds) at which the destruction of the owner (GameObject) is checked by polling.
Maximum number of retries when a load fails.
When turned off, this rule is treated as nonexistent in auto registration, in conflict detection and in the "covered by auto registration" check of manual bulk registration.
The target folder (a folder inside Assets). Drag the folder asset to specify it. It is held by GUID, so renaming or moving it does not break the link.
How targets are specified: by extensions, or everything that can be registered (All).
Extensions to target (used in the extension mode). If empty, nothing is registered.
Exclude patterns (glob, e.g. **/_Test/**). Anything that matches is not targeted, even under the target folder.
Address template. Macros can be used. If empty, the asset path is used.
Name (template) of the target group. Macros can be used. If empty, the Addressables DefaultGroup is used.
The Addressables Group Template used to create a new group when the target group does not exist. If empty, the Group Template of the Editor SO is used.
Labels (multiple; macros can be used). If empty, no label is added.
How the address behaves when an asset is moved or renamed. Follow re-expands the template; Fixed keeps the address once registered.
